Summary: Usability and Account Management
Description: Easier navigation, richer attendance views, class sheet downloads and password management for admin, teacher and student.

Summary: As a user, I want a left-side menu with all my options so that I can reach every page quickly.
Description: Acceptance criteria: After login the admin, teacher and student each see a left sidebar with only their own options; the current page is highlighted; the layout also works on a small screen; the login page uses the same clean design.

Summary: Design sidebar layout and colour scheme
Build shared sidebar fragment for the three roles
Apply the new layout to all existing pages and the login page
Test sidebar links for each role and on a small screen
As a user, I want to change my own password and see what I type so that my account stays safe.
Description: Acceptance criteria: Any logged-in user can change their password by entering the current password and a new password of at least 6 characters twice; a wrong current password is rejected; password fields have a show password option; the login page has a Forgot password link that tells the user to contact the admin; the admin can set a new temporary password for any student or teacher.

Summary: Build change password page and service
Add show/hide password option to login and password forms
Add forgot password page and admin reset password button
Test password change and reset and login with the new password
As a student, I want a dashboard and a detailed attendance page so that I can see how I am doing and what to improve.
Description: Acceptance criteria: The student dashboard shows overall attendance percentage and the number of subjects at risk; the attendance page shows for each subject the teacher, present, late, absent, total, percentage, a status label and the classes needed to reach 75%; the student can filter by subject and by date range.

Summary: Design student dashboard and attendance page
Add present/late/absent counts and overall percentage to the report logic
Add classes needed to reach 75% calculation
Add subject and date range filters
Test numbers against manual counts
As a teacher, I want a dashboard and better report filters so that I can quickly find students who need attention.
Description: Acceptance criteria: The teacher dashboard lists my classes and shows which subjects have attendance taken today; the class report shows present, late, absent, total and percentage; the report can be filtered by class and subject, date range, name or roll number, only students below 75%, and sorted.

Summary: Design teacher dashboard
Add present/late/absent columns to the class report
Add search and below-75% and sort filters
Test filters with sample data
As a teacher, I want to download an attendance sheet for one class so that I can keep or print it.
Description: Acceptance criteria: The teacher chooses a class and subject and an optional date range and downloads an Excel file with one row per student and one column per class date marked P, A or L, plus totals and percentage; dates show correctly and never as ####; a teacher can download only their own subjects. Change request: the admin CSV export (AT-42) is removed because teachers now own the download.

Summary: Add Excel library and build the sheet generator
Add download page for the teacher
Remove the admin CSV export page (change request replacing AT-42)
Fix #### date display seen in the old CSV
Test that the downloaded file opens with correct dates and totals
As an admin, I want a summary dashboard and student filters so that I can manage many students easily.
Description: Acceptance criteria: The admin dashboard shows the number of students, teachers, classes and subjects; the student list can be filtered by class and by status (active or deactivated) and searched by name or roll number.

Summary: Add count tiles to the admin dashboard
Add class and status and search filters to the student list
Test the filters
Load batch data: classes, teachers, subjects and student logins
Description: Set up the data for the demo: classes, 6 teachers, 5 subjects and student accounts created from the college batch list. Setup work, not a user story, so no story points.
